items.title: BoundInk: Boundary-Aware Online Handwriting Generation
items.text: Realistic online handwriting depends not only on individual character shapes, but also on how a writer connects, spaces, and aligns adjacent characters. Existing methods rely primarily on long-range sequence modeling and capture these inter-character behaviors only implicitly. This often produces plausible glyphs accompanied by broken cursive joins, inconsistent spacing, or writer-inconsistent transitions. We introduce BoundInk, a writer-conditioned framework that treats inter-character boundaries as explicit generation units. By jointly modeling local transitions and surrounding text context, BoundInk preserves writer-specific glyph appearance while improving connectivity and spacing across complete text lines. We further introduce a boundary-aware evaluation framework that directly assesses cursive continuity and spatial relationships between characters beyond conventional trajectory similarity. Across three benchmark-matched settings, BoundInk improves all applicable boundary-quality measures and reduces normalized dynamic time warping by 17.6--47.8%. In blind human evaluations, BoundInk outputs are preferred in 78.0--82.6% of valid criterion-wise judgments.

items.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance
items.text: Long-horizon reasoning remains a central challenge for large language models (LLMs) under sparse-reward regimes. We argue that this brittleness arises from two biases induced by complex reasoning spaces: an exploration bias, where models are drawn toward locally plausible but structurally unstable branches, and a compounding bias, where small local deviations accumulate across depth and suppress rare rewards. items.text: A main promise of looped language models is depth-adaptive inference. By looping a block of shared layers a variable number of times, the model can use less compute for "easy" tokens and more for "hard" ones. items.text: Time series agents answer analytical questions by calling external tools, and which tools they carry is decided by people before the agent runs. However, we identify two failures in this setup. To address this, we propose TimeEvo, which clusters an agent's diagnosed failures into capability gaps, plans a measurement for each, synthesizes evidence-only tools that fill them, and admits the candidate library only through a paired admission gate. items.title: A Safety-Bounded SDC-to-MCP Gateway for Medical AI Agents
items.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a common interface through which AI applications discover and use external resources and tools. It allows language-model agents to ground their reasoning in current system state and interact with heterogeneous services. In medical environments, however, exposing device state and action affordances requires deterministic constraints on possible effects. We present an IEEE 11073 Service-Oriented Device Connectivity (SDC)-to-MCP gateway that exposes metrics, alarms, context references, and semantic metadata as read-only resources, while representing selected action affordances as policy-validated dry-run tools. The term safety-bounded denotes a narrow no-execution property: agent-facing requests dispatch no SDC device operation. A Python prototype supports simulated fault and lifecycle experiments, a software-reference protocol path spanning independent Java and Python implementations, deterministic baselines, representation ablations, and multi-model agent evaluation. items.text:
What if everything goes right?



Every day, I’ll take one startup from @lennysan’s top 100 list and sketch out the most ambitious case I can for its future.



How it started, what it's building, how big it could get if everything tips its way.



Day one: @AbridgeHQ 



Founding Story: Abridge was founded in 2018 by @ShivdevRao,  Sandeep Konam and Florian Metze to help patients record, reflect and follow through on conversations with healthcare practitioners. USV led its Series A on this thesis. 



In August 2022, it raised a Series A-1 from Wittington Ventures and announced a pivot to enterprise, competing with the leading player in the medical transcription space, Nuance, and its DAX ambient listening product (I was a large public investor in Nuance during my Coatue days on the thesis that DAX was the future!). It has grown explosively since and has raised $750m+ of venture and growth funding. 



Product Vision: At the simplest level, Abridge is a sensor company- its product transcribes medical conversations and turns them into concrete takeaways, notes, etc. 



This gives it both unique data and an entry point in millions of medical conversations. Beyond the obvious benefits of saving physicians time and increasing note accuracy, Abridge is working to bring ambient intelligence to visits- both for medical purposes and for billing/revenue cycle purposes. Abridge's contextual reasoning engine merges insurance company requirements, updated medical literature, etc. to create both the best possible post-visit note and the right, context-aware explanation to insurance companies. 



Stats:



* 300+ live health systems (as of September 2026)

* 100m+ projected patient-clinician interactions in 2026

* 678 employees, per LinkedIn, up 44% Y/y

* $758m raised

* $5.3b last round valuation (Series E in June 2025)

* Backed by a16Z, Khosla, Elad Gil, IVP, Bessemer, Lightspeed, etc. 



Bull Case:



Ambient note-taking in healthcare settings is both inevitable and a bankable constant. As long as doctors and nurses see patients in person, they'll need to record and process the content of those conversations. That gives Abridge a live microphone in the room where valuable, high-stakes decisions are made.



Online sources estimate pricing for core scribing tools runs ~$250/clinician/month or $3k/year, leading to a ~$3b revenue TAM from the core product alone in the US, where about 1m doctors practice today.



But that's just the start. 



Abridge sits on a unique opportunity to move from ambient to proactive over time, especially as voice AI improves its conversational skills. Patient visits are crucial moments and a missed step can be costly medically and financially. If a patient is referred for, say, back surgery without the prerequisite care her insurance requires, a mess of paperwork can ensue- and if a doctor happens to be out of date on the best treatment course or research, patients may get less than the care they deserve.



In the bull case for Abridge, hospitals and practices start to treat the data from their doctor-patient interactions with the same analytical rigor that high-performing companies apply to sales calls- looking for ways to improve them, finding key questions that went unasked, follow-ups that need to be taken care of, providing coaching, etc. 



Moving from ambient documentation to clinical augmentation isn't easy, but in this scenario Abridge becomes a third participant in doctor-patient interactions, jumping in with full context if something important is missing, recommending follow-ups, surfacing up-to-date best practices, etc. In the not-too-distant future, it will probably be unimaginable that we used to have such critical conversations one-on-one with our doctors rather than having a tool like Abridge watching out for us in the background.

items.title: C3M: Cross-Session Multimodal Memory Maintenance for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.text: Long-horizon tasks require preserving and later recovering cross-session evidence under a bounded, query-blind memory budget. Existing compression can discard fine-grained visual cues or conflate semantically similar but incompatible observations. We present C3M, a cross-session multimodal memory organization that maintains a bounded active index over persistent source text-image evidence. Relation-aware updates consolidate safe redundancy while preserving complementary and incompatible records. At query time, budgeted routing selects useful index pages and expands their associated source evidence under a fixed reader budget. Together, these mechanisms establish a compact, provenance-preserving multimodal memory organization for cross-session long-horizon tasks, retaining temporal distinctions and source links required for reliable downstream reasoning.
